1	# Global Renewable Energy in 2025: How Far Have We Come?
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	Our World in Data – Renewable Energy  
     6	URL: https://ourworldindata.org/renewable-energy  
     7	Authors: Hannah Ritchie, Max Roser, Pablo Rosado  
     8	Data sources: Ember (2026); Energy Institute – Statistical Review of World Energy (2025)
     9	
    10	## The Urgency: Why Renewables Matter
    11	
    12	Since the Industrial Revolution, most countries' energy systems have become dominated by fossil fuels. Three-quarters of global greenhouse gas emissions come from burning fossil fuels for energy. Fossil fuel combustion is also responsible for local air pollution that causes at least 5 million premature deaths per year. To reduce CO₂ emissions and air pollution, the world must rapidly shift toward low-carbon energy sources — nuclear and renewable technologies.
    13	
    14	Renewable energy includes solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal, bioenergy, wave, and tidal sources. Traditional biomass (important in lower-income settings) is typically excluded from modern renewable statistics.
    15	
    16	## Renewables in the Primary Energy Mix
    17	
    18	Approximately one-seventh (~14%) of the world's primary energy now comes from renewable technologies (2024 data, substitution method). Primary energy encompasses electricity, transport, and heating combined. Because transport and heating are harder to decarbonize (more reliant on oil and gas), the renewable share in the total energy mix is lower than in the electricity mix alone.
    19	
    20	![Share of primary energy from renewables by country, 2024](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    21	
    22	Regional variation is significant. Countries like Norway, Brazil, and New Zealand derive large shares of primary energy from renewables, while fossil-fuel-producing nations in the Middle East and parts of Asia remain below 5%.
    23	
    24	## Renewables in the Electricity Mix
    25	
    26	Globally, almost one-third of electricity now comes from renewable sources (2025). This is substantially higher than the primary energy share because electricity is the sector where renewables have made the most progress.
    27	
    28	![Share of electricity from renewables by country, 2025](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    29	
    30	| Region / Country | Renewable Share of Electricity (approx.) |
    31	|---|---|
    32	| Norway | ~98% |
    33	| Brazil | ~85% |
    34	| Canada | ~65% |
    35	| Germany | ~55% |
    36	| China | ~35% |
    37	| United States | ~25% |
    38	| India | ~25% |
    39	| World average | ~30% |
    40	| Saudi Arabia | <2% |
    41	| South Africa | ~10% |
    42	
    43	Several African and Middle Eastern countries have renewable electricity shares below 10%, reflecting both fossil fuel dependence and limited investment in renewables.
    44	
    45	## Breakdown by Technology: Hydro, Wind, and Solar
    46	
    47	**Hydropower** remains the single largest renewable electricity source, accounting for roughly half of all renewable generation. It has been generating electricity at scale for over a century. Top producers include China, Brazil, and Canada.
    48	
    49	![Hydropower generation by country, 2025](./assets/figure_6.jpg)
    50	
    51	**Wind energy** has grown rapidly and is now a major contributor, especially in Europe, China, and the United States. Wind generation includes both onshore and offshore installations.
    52	
    53	![Wind power generation by country, 2025](./assets/figure_8.jpg)
    54	
    55	**Solar energy** is the fastest-growing source. Global solar generation has increased dramatically since 2010, driven by falling costs and policy support.
    56	
    57	| Technology | Approx. Global Generation (2024, TWh) | Share of Renewable Electricity |
    58	|---|---|---|
    59	| Hydropower | ~4,500 | ~47% |
    60	| Wind | ~2,400 | ~25% |
    61	| Solar | ~2,000 | ~21% |
    62	| Other renewables (geothermal, biomass, wave, tidal) | ~700 | ~7% |
    63	
    64	While hydropower still leads, wind and solar combined now nearly match hydro's output and are growing much faster.
    65	
    66	## Access and Regional Disparities
    67	
    68	The transition to renewables is highly uneven. Scandinavian countries, Brazil, and Canada benefit from abundant hydropower. European nations like Denmark and Germany have invested heavily in wind and solar. Meanwhile, much of Sub-Saharan Africa has minimal renewable electricity infrastructure, and many Middle Eastern nations remain almost entirely dependent on fossil fuels for electricity.
    69	
    70	![Share of electricity from hydropower by country, 2025](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    71	
    72	## Key Findings
    73	
    74	- **~14% of global primary energy** and **~30% of global electricity** now come from renewable sources — a significant milestone but far from sufficient for climate targets.
    75	- **Hydropower remains dominant**, generating roughly half of all renewable electricity, but its growth potential is limited compared to wind and solar.
    76	- **Wind and solar are the fastest-growing energy technologies** in history; combined, they now produce nearly as much electricity as hydropower.
    77	- **Stark regional disparities persist**: Scandinavia and Latin America exceed 60–90% renewable electricity, while much of the Middle East and Sub-Saharan Africa remain below 10%.
    78	- **Transport and heating lag far behind electricity** in the renewable transition, keeping the overall primary energy share much lower than the electricity share.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# Create presentation with 16:9 aspect ratio
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette - data-forward, analytical, accessible
DARK_BLUE = RgbColor(0x1A, 0x2E, 0x4A)      # Primary dark
TEAL = RgbColor(0x2E, 0x8B, 0x8B)           # Accent
LIGHT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xF5, 0xF5, 0xF5)     # Background
WHITE = RgbColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
DARK_TEXT = RgbColor(0x33, 0x33, 0x33)
MEDIUM_GRAY = RgbColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88)
CHART_BLUE = RgbColor(0x1F, 0x4E, 0x79)
CHART_GREEN = RgbColor(0x2E, 0x8B, 0x57)
CHART_ORANGE = RgbColor(0xD4, 0x6A, 0x1E)
CHART_PURPLE = RgbColor(0x6B, 0x4C, 0x9A)

ASSETS_DIR = "/app/benchmark/assets"

def add_background(slide, color=LIGHT_GRAY):
    background = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, prs.slide_width, prs.slide_height
    )
    background.fill.solid()
    background.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    background.line.fill.background()
    # Send to back
    spTree = slide.shapes._spTree
    sp = background._element
    spTree.remove(sp)
    spTree.insert(2, sp)

def add_title_bar(slide, title_text, subtitle_text=None):
    # Title bar background
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, prs.slide_width, Inches(1.4)
    )
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
    bar.line.fill.background()
    
    # Title text
    title_box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(0.25), Inches(12.333), Inches(0.7))
    tf = title_box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = title_text
    p.font.size = Pt(32)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    
    if subtitle_text:
        p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
        p2.text = subtitle_text
        p2.font.size = Pt(14)
        p2.font.color.rgb = RgbColor(0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC)
        p2.font.name = "Calibri"
        p2.space_before = Pt(4)

def add_footer(slide, source_text="Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy (Ember 2026; Energy Institute 2025)"):
    footer = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(7.1), Inches(12.333), Inches(0.3))
    tf = footer.text_frame
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = source_text
    p.font.size = Pt(9)
    p.font.color.rgb = MEDIUM_GRAY
    p.font.name = "Calibri"

def add_bullet_text(slide, bullets, left=Inches(0.5), top=Inches(1.7), width=Inches(12.333), height=Inches(5.2), font_size=Pt(18)):
    box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = "• " + bullet
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
        p.space_after = Pt(14)
        p.level = 0
    return box

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 1: Title Slide
# ============================================================
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # blank
add_background(slide1, DARK_BLUE)

# Title
title_box = slide1.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.333), Inches(1.5))
tf = title_box.text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True
p = tf.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "Global Renewable Energy in 2025"
p.font.size = Pt(48)
p.font.bold = True
p.font.color.rgb = WHITE
p.font.name = "Calibri"
p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
p2.text = "How Far Have We Come?"
p2.font.size = Pt(36)
p2.font.color.rgb = TEAL
p2.font.name = "Calibri"
p2.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
p2.space_before = Pt(12)

# Subtitle
sub_box = slide1.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(4.2), Inches(11.333), Inches(1))
tf2 = sub_box.text_frame
tf2.word_wrap = True
p3 = tf2.paragraphs[0]
p3.text = "A data-driven overview of renewable energy's growing share in global energy and electricity"
p3.font.size = Pt(18)
p3.font.color.rgb = RgbColor(0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC)
p3.font.name = "Calibri"
p3.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

# Source attribution
src_box = slide1.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(1), Inches(6.2), Inches(11.333), Inches(0.8))
tf3 = src_box.text_frame
tf3.word_wrap = True
p4 = tf3.paragraphs[0]
p4.text = "Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy"
p4.font.size = Pt(12)
p4.font.color.rgb = RgbColor(0x99, 0x99, 0x99)
p4.font.name = "Calibri"
p4.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

p5 = tf3.add_paragraph()
p5.text = "Data: Ember (2026); Energy Institute – Statistical Review of World Energy (2025)"
p5.font.size = Pt(11)
p5.font.color.rgb = RgbColor(0x77, 0x77, 0x77)
p5.font.name = "Calibri"
p5.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
p5.space_before = Pt(4)

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 2: Fossil Fuel Dominance Context
# ============================================================
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide2)
add_title_bar(slide2, "75% of Global GHG Emissions Still Come from Fossil Fuels")
add_footer(slide2)

bullets = [
    "Since the Industrial Revolution, fossil fuels have dominated global energy systems.",
    "Three-quarters of global greenhouse gas emissions come from burning fossil fuels for energy.",
    "Fossil fuel combustion causes at least 5 million premature deaths per year from local air pollution.",
    "To reduce CO₂ emissions and air pollution, the world must rapidly shift toward low-carbon sources — nuclear and renewable technologies.",
    "Renewable energy includes solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal, bioenergy, wave, and tidal sources."
]
add_bullet_text(slide2, bullets, top=Inches(1.7), font_size=Pt(20))

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 3: Renewables in Primary Energy (~14%)
# ============================================================
slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide3)
add_title_bar(slide3, "Renewables Now Supply ~14% of Global Primary Energy", "Primary energy encompasses electricity, transport, and heating combined (2024 data, substitution method)")
add_footer(slide3)

# Left: key stats
stats_box = slide3.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.7), Inches(4.5), Inches(2.5))
tf = stats_box.text_frame
tf.word_wrap = True
p = tf.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "Key Insight"
p.font.size = Pt(20)
p.font.bold = True
p.font.color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
p.font.name = "Calibri"

p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
p2.text = "Approximately one-seventh of the world's primary energy now comes from renewable technologies."
p2.font.size = Pt(16)
p2.font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
p2.font.name = "Calibri"
p2.space_before = Pt(10)

p3 = tf.add_paragraph()
p3.text = "Because transport and heating are harder to decarbonize, the renewable share in total energy is lower than in electricity alone."
p3.font.size = Pt(14)
p3.font.color.rgb = MEDIUM_GRAY
p3.font.name = "Calibri"
p3.space_before = Pt(10)

# Right: figure_2.jpg
slide3.shapes.add_picture(os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "figure_2.jpg"), Inches(5.2), Inches(1.7), width=Inches(7.6))

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 4: Renewable Electricity Generation Growth (bar chart)
# ============================================================
slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide4)
add_title_bar(slide4, "Renewable Electricity Generation Is Growing Rapidly, Led by Wind and Solar")
add_footer(slide4)

# Data table
slide4.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.6), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.4)).text_frame.paragraphs[0].text = "Global Renewable Generation by Technology (2024)"
slide4.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.6), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.4)).text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(14)
slide4.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.6), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.4)).text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
slide4.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.6), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.4)).text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = DARK_BLUE

# Build table
rows, cols = 5, 3
table_left = Inches(0.5)
table_top = Inches(2.0)
table_width = Inches(4.5)
table_height = Inches(2.2)
table = slide4.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, table_left, table_top, table_width, table_height).table

table.cell(0, 0).text = "Technology"
table.cell(0, 1).text = "Generation (TWh)"
table.cell(0, 2).text = "Share of Renewables"

table.cell(1, 0).text = "Hydropower"
table.cell(1, 1).text = "~4,500"
table.cell(1, 2).text = "~47%"

table.cell(2, 0).text = "Wind"
table.cell(2, 1).text = "~2,400"
table.cell(2, 2).text = "~25%"

table.cell(3, 0).text = "Solar"
table.cell(3, 1).text = "~2,000"
table.cell(3, 2).text = "~21%"

table.cell(4, 0).text = "Other renewables"
table.cell(4, 1).text = "~700"
table.cell(4, 2).text = "~7%"

for row in range(rows):
    for col in range(cols):
        cell = table.cell(row, col)
        cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(13)
        cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.name = "Calibri"
        if row == 0:
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BLUE
            cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = WHITE
            cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
        else:
            cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT

# Bar chart (manual shapes)
chart_left = Inches(5.5)
chart_top = Inches(1.8)
chart_width = Inches(7.0)
chart_height = Inches(4.8)

data = [("Hydropower", 4500, CHART_BLUE), ("Wind", 2400, CHART_GREEN), ("Solar", 2000, CHART_ORANGE), ("Other", 700, CHART_PURPLE)]
max_val = 5000
bar_width = Inches(1.2)
spacing = Inches(1.6)

for i, (label, value, color) in enumerate(data):
    bar_height = (value / max_val) * chart_height
    bar_left = chart_left + i * spacing
    bar_top = chart_top + chart_height - bar_height
    
    bar = slide4.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, bar_left, bar_top, bar_width, bar_height)
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    bar.line.fill.background()
    
    # Value label
    val_box = slide4.shapes.add_textbox(bar_left, bar_top - Inches(0.3), bar_width, Inches(0.25))
    val_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].text = f"{value:,} TWh"
    val_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(12)
    val_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
    val_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
    val_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
    
    # Category label
    cat_box = slide4.shapes.add_textbox(bar_left, chart_top + chart_height + Inches(0.05), bar_width, Inches(0.3))
    cat_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].text = label
    cat_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(12)
    cat_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
    cat_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

# Insight text below chart
insight_box = slide4.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(5.5), Inches(6.5), Inches(7.0), Inches(0.5))
insight_box.text_frame.word_wrap = True
insight_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].text = "Wind and solar combined (~4,400 TWh) now nearly match hydropower's output and are growing much faster."
insight_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(13)
insight_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
insight_box.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.italic = True

# ============================================================
# SLIDE 5: Electricity Mix ~One-Third Renewable + table
# ============================================================
slide5 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
add_background(slide5)
add_title_bar(slide5, "Almost One-Third of Global Electricity Now Comes from Renewables")
add_footer(slide5)

# Left: map figure_1.jpg
slide5.shapes.add_picture(os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "figure_1.jpg"), Inches(0.4), Inches(1.7), width=Inches(7.8))

# Right: data table of selected countries
table_left = Inches(8.4)
table_top = Inches(1.8)
table_width = Inches(4.4)
table_height = Inches(4.0)
rows, cols = 7, 2
table2 = slide5.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, table_left, table_top, table_width, table_height).table

table2.cell(0, 0).text = "Country / Region"
table2.cell(0, 1).text = "Renewable Share"

countries = [
    ("Norway", "~98%"),
    ("Brazil", "~85%"),
    ("Canada", "~65%"),
